generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, step 1, unique per table; never NULL; generated PKs are offset above max(compact PK) and deduped against the compact key set.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_amount: Uniform integer in [0, 100000] scaled to the column's scale; never negative; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_rate: Uniform in [0, 1] with the column's scale; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random uppercase letters/digits of length 2-10; near-variants (case flips, one-char edits) for equality/LIKE literals; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random capitalized word of length 3-20; duplicates allowed on non-unique columns; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date: Uniform date in [1980-01-01, 2010-12-31]; format %Y-%m-%d; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.phone: Pattern 'NNN.NNN.NNNN' with random digits; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.email: Uppercase letters derived from first/last name, unique per table; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_column: Copy a value from the parent table's final key pool (after PK dedup, NULL rule, and exclusion of RESERVED_UNMATCHED keys); include NULL rows when the column is nullable; include parent rows with no children.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, emit L-1, L, L+1 (by column step).
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_date: For each listed literal D, emit D-1 day, D, D+1 day.
generic_sampling_rules.near_variant_text: For each listed literal S, emit S, lower(S), upper(S), and one single-character edit.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_order: Emit at least two rows sharing the same value at the listed ORDER rank.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_distinct: Emit duplicate values on the DISTINCT column at the listed share; planted duplicates are type-aware (phone-shaped for PHONE_NUMBER, name-shaped for LAST_NAME, title-shaped for JOB_TITLE).
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns emit at least one NULL row and non-NULL rows; share per compact DB (5-30% for manager_id); default share (0.05, 0.20) for nullable columns without an explicit NULL_SHARE entry.

generation_specification.uncertainty: Original sample contains invalid rows (job_history START_DATE '0000-00-00', employees MANAGER_ID 0, DEPARTMENT_ID 0/90/100 not in departments, locations COUNTRY_ID not in countries); generation enforces FK integrity and drops these. Region names trimmed of trailing \r. COMMISSION_PCT null_rate reported 0 but column is nullable; NULL rows are still generated per instruction 10. table_sizes_per_instance is the target generated-row count appended to a copy of the compact DB; compact rows are never deleted or changed, and jitter is not applied (choose_table_sizes must use the fixed sizes). After all parent tables are finalized (PK dedup, unique dedup, NULL rule), every child FK column is re-sampled or filtered against the final parent key set; NULL_FK_CHILD columns keep at least one NULL. _apply_null_rule runs after all FK fills and formula enforcement, and formula re-draws never replace a planted NULL. _apply_unmatched_parent reserves at least one parent row with no children and at least one child FK NULL where nullable; the FK fill must exclude RESERVED_UNMATCHED keys from the parent pool so the reserved parent truly has no children. _apply_group_sizes operates only on non-PK grouping columns (departments.DEPARTMENT_NAME); it is never applied to a primary-key column. The writer receives orig_path so each unit file is a copy of the compact DB with generated rows appended; the writer's rows_ok/rows_failed are propagated into the summary and a unit fails if any rows_failed or if the output is not a superset of the compact DB. The post-write integrity check must not fail on pre-existing compact-row violations: it compares the written file's FK/NOT NULL/PK violation set against the original compact DB's violation set and fails only on new violations introduced by generated rows (or equivalently runs the check on a fresh in-memory DB containing only generated rows).

issues.title: Generated instances are invalid: compact rows missing and new FK violations
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.valid=0, invalid=20; reasons.compact_rows_missing=20, new_integrity_failures=20, no_rows_added=19; integrity.fk_violations=1400. writer.write_instance_sqlite is called from cli._one as write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) with orig_path defaulting to None, so the compact DB is never copied (the `if orig_path and os.path.exists(orig_path)` branch is skipped) and only generated rows are inserted. Generated FK columns are drawn from schema.original_values (compact values) plus generated parents, but since compact rows are absent, every FK pointing at a compact-only parent value becomes a violation. This directly contradicts the spec's 'compact rows are never deleted or changed' and the stated intent that instances are 'a copy of the compact database plus appended generated rows'.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original DB path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the args dict in cli.main and forward it in _one), so each unit file is a copy of the compact DB with generated rows appended. Re-run and confirm validity.valid>0, compact_rows_missing=0, and fk_violations=0.

issues.title: FK consistency is broken by post-sampling PK dedup and NULL application
issues.evidence: In instance.build_random_instance, fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws child FKs from the parent pool, but afterwards sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates drop parent rows, and _apply_null_rule sets parent PK/NOT NULL columns to NULL only for non-PK columns (PKs are skipped, good), yet the self-FK fixup loop only repairs FKs where pt == t. Cross-table FKs (employees.DEPARTMENT_ID -> departments, employees.JOB_ID -> jobs, job_history.*, locations.COUNTRY_ID, departments.LOCATION_ID) are never re-validated after parent rows are dropped, so child values can reference deleted parents. Combined with the missing compact copy this yields the 1400 FK violations observed.
issues.requested_revision: After all parent tables are finalized (PK dedup, unique dedup, NULL rule), re-sample or filter every child FK column against the final parent key set (not just self-FKs), and ensure NULL_FK_CHILD columns still contain at least one NULL. Add an assertion in the writer or a post-build check that every non-NULL FK value exists in the parent column.

issues.title: Specified NULL share and NULL presence not honored for several nullable columns
issues.evidence: Feedback nullable_columns shows 'countries.REGION_ID: NULL 0/29', 'departments.LOCATION_ID: NULL 0/1', 'departments.MANAGER_ID: NULL 0/1', 'jobs.MAX_SALARY: NULL 0/5', 'jobs.MIN_SALARY: NULL 0/5'. The spec's null_targets lists all of these as nullable and the interface rule requires at least one NULL per nullable column per instance. _apply_null_rule only runs on columns present in `cols` and skips cm.pk_pos>0, but for FK columns filled by fill_foreign_keys_consistently the values are added to `cols` after the sampler loop, and _apply_null_rule is called after that — however for departments.LOCATION_ID/MANAGER_ID the table has only 1 generated row (jittered size), so k=max(1,round(share*1))=1 but rng.sample(range(1),1) sets the single row to NULL, which then gets overwritten by the self-FK fixup or by the FK fill ordering. For jobs.MIN/MAX_SALARY the formula re-draw replaces NULL with a non-NULL pool value (see _apply_formulas: 'a violating value is re-drawn (never NULL-replaced)' — but it also replaces NULLs because the formula returns True for None, so this is not the cause; the cause is that _apply_null_rule runs before _apply_formulas and the formula's re-draw pool excludes None, so a NULL that fails a formula is replaced).
issues.requested_revision: Ensure _apply_null_rule runs after all FK fills and formula enforcement, and that formula re-draws never replace a planted NULL (skip re-draw when v is None). Verify each nullable column has >=1 NULL and a share within the compact share per instance.

issues.title: Specification's 'unmatched_join_rows' and 'group_sizes' are not actually constructed
issues.evidence: spec.UNMATCHED_PARENT is declared but instance._apply_unmatched_parent is a documented no-op ('nothing to do here ... arise naturally'). spec.GROUP_SIZES is applied by _apply_group_sizes, but it only plants values on the first 6 rows of the grouping column and does not guarantee the target profile [1,2,3] survives PK dedup or that the grouping column is the PK (for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID the PK dedup may drop the planted duplicates). The spec's per_column_exceptions require 'parent_rows_without_children' and 'child_rows_with_null_fk' for departments/employees, and group sizes '1,2,>=3' for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID, departments.DEPARTMENT_NAME, job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID. The construction_pairs feedback shows only 46/106 separated, with no group breakdown, so these patterns are not demonstrably realized.
issues.requested_revision: Either implement _apply_unmatched_parent to explicitly reserve at least one parent row with no children (and at least one child FK NULL for NULL_FK_CHILD), and make _apply_group_sizes operate on a non-PK grouping column or after PK dedup, or remove these patterns from the specification if they are not intended to be constructed. Add a post-build check that reports realized group-size profiles and unmatched-parent counts.

issues.title: Specification claims compact rows are preserved but program appends only; ambiguity in 'table_sizes_per_instance'
issues.evidence: Spec table_sizes_per_instance gives exact sizes (regions 4, countries 25, ..., employees 107, job_history 11) matching the compact DB, but instance.choose_table_sizes applies a jitter of ±base//4 and clamps to [0,230], so generated row counts differ from the spec. The spec's uncertainty note says 'generation enforces FK integrity and drops these' (invalid compact rows), which conflicts with the program's stated 'compact rows are never deleted or changed'. The feedback shows no_rows_added=19, meaning generated rows were not appended at all in most instances (because the compact copy was skipped and the writer inserted only generated rows, which then failed or were empty).
issues.requested_revision: Clarify whether table_sizes_per_instance is the target generated-row count or the total row count, and whether jitter is allowed. If compact rows must be preserved, state that explicitly and remove the 'drops these' language. Align choose_table_sizes with the clarified spec.

issues.title: Reproducibility and error reporting are weak
issues.evidence: cli._one catches all exceptions and returns only the exception type name; the summary prints 'rows_added': {} and 'rows_skipped': {} as empty dicts, so the writer's return value ({'rows_ok','rows_failed'}) is discarded. The feedback reports n_ok=20, n_fail=0 but validity.valid=0, so the CLI's success signal is misleading. Reproducibility is claimed true, but the seed is seed_base*100003+i and rng is per-unit, which is fine; however the missing orig_path means the output is not a copy of the compact DB, so 'reproducible' only means the same wrong output.
issues.requested_revision: Propagate the writer's rows_ok/rows_failed into the summary, and treat a unit as failed if the writer reports any rows_failed or if the output file is not a superset of the compact DB. Add a post-write integrity check (FK, NOT NULL, PK) and fail the unit if it does not pass.

unresolved_checks: Whether the 46/106 separated construction pairs are sufficient for the intended value variation; the feedback gives no per-group breakdown, so it is not possible to confirm which patterns (boundary, group_sizes, unmatched_join, null_rows, duplicates_for_distinct, ties_for_order_limit) are realized.

Whether the compact DB's actual NULL shares per nullable column match the spec's NULL_SHARE (only employees.MANAGER_ID is specified as 5-30%; others default to 5-20% in _apply_null_rule, which may not match the compact share).
Whether the spec's 'uncertainty' note about dropping invalid compact rows is intended to override the 'compact rows are never deleted' statement; this needs designer clarification.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units fail with RuntimeError('post-write integrity check failed'); n_ok=0, n_instances=0. The integrity check in writer.py `_integrity_ok` runs `pragma foreign_key_check`, NOT NULL checks, and PK duplicate checks on the written file. The generated rows are appended to a copy of the compact DB whose original rows are known to violate integrity (spec uncertainty: 'Original sample contains invalid rows ... employees MANAGER_ID 0, DEPARTMENT_ID 0/90/100 not in departments, locations COUNTRY_ID not in countries'). Since compact rows are never deleted or changed (per spec), `pragma foreign_key_check` will always report the pre-existing violations, so the integrity check can never pass.
issues.requested_revision: The post-write integrity check must not fail on pre-existing compact-row violations that the spec explicitly says are retained. Either (a) restrict the FK/NOT NULL/PK check to only the appended generated rows (e.g. compare against the original compact DB's violation set and only fail on new violations), or (b) run the integrity check on a fresh in-memory DB containing only generated rows, or (c) exclude the known-invalid compact rows from the check. The check must still catch genuine generation errors (new FK/NOT NULL/PK violations introduced by generated rows).

issues.evidence: instance.py `_apply_unmatched_parent` records a reserved key in `spec.RESERVED_UNMATCHED`, but `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` and `_revalidate_fks` never consult `RESERVED_UNMATCHED` when drawing FK values. The docstring says 'the FK fill consults it' but the code does not. Therefore the 'parent_rows_without_children' target for departments/jobs/employees is not guaranteed by construction.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK fills exclude the reserved unmatched parent keys from the parent pool (or otherwise guarantee at least one parent row with no children), so the unmatched_join_rows 'parent_rows_without_children' target is actually enforced.

issues.evidence: spec.py `NULL_FK_CHILD = {('employees', 'DEPARTMENT_ID')}` and the spec requires 'child_rows_with_null_fk' for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID and employees.DEPARTMENT_ID unmatched_join_rows. However, `_apply_null_rule` only nulls columns where `cm.notnull` is false and `cm.pk_pos == 0`; it does not specifically guarantee a NULL in the FK child column, and `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` fills all FK columns with non-NULL parent values. The 'child_rows_with_null_fk' target is not explicitly enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Explicitly plant at least one NULL in each child FK column listed in the unmatched_join_rows targets (employees.DEPARTMENT_ID, and departments.DEPARTMENT_ID where applicable) after FK fill, and ensure the NULL rule does not overwrite it.

issues.evidence: spec.py `GROUP_SIZES` includes ('departments','DEPARTMENT_ID') and ('departments','DEPARTMENT_NAME'), but `_apply_group_sizes` runs after `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` and mutates values in place without re-checking PK/unique dedup. For departments.DEPARTMENT_ID (the PK), forcing group sizes 1,2,>=3 by overwriting values can create duplicate PKs, which would then fail the PK integrity check. Also the spec's uncertainty states '_apply_group_sizes operates on a non-PK grouping column or after PK dedup' — but the code applies it to the PK column DEPARTMENT_ID.
issues.requested_revision: Do not apply group_sizes to a primary-key column (departments.DEPARTMENT_ID); restrict group_sizes to non-PK grouping columns (e.g. DEPARTMENT_NAME), or re-run PK dedup after group-size application and verify no duplicate PKs remain.

issues.evidence: The spec's `table_sizes_per_instance` gives fixed counts (regions 4, countries 25, ...), but instance.py `choose_table_sizes` applies jitter (`rng.randint(-base//4, base//4)`) and the spec uncertainty says 'jitter is not applied'. This is a direct contradiction between the specification text and the program.
issues.requested_revision: Either remove the jitter from `choose_table_sizes` to match the fixed `table_sizes_per_instance`, or update the specification to state that jitter is applied. The spec uncertainty explicitly says jitter is not applied, so the program should be changed to use the fixed sizes.

issues.evidence: The spec's `null_targets` lists many nullable columns (e.g. employees.COMMISSION_PCT, employees.FIRST_NAME, employees.PHONE_NUMBER, employees.SALARY, departments.MANAGER_ID, departments.LOCATION_ID, job_history.DEPARTMENT_ID, locations.COUNTRY_ID, etc.), and the NULL rule requires each nullable column to have at least one NULL row per instance. The program's `_apply_null_rule` does enforce >=1 NULL for all nullable non-PK columns, which is consistent. However, the spec's uncertainty notes 'COMMISSION_PCT null_rate reported 0 but column is nullable; NULL rows are still generated per instruction 10' — this is consistent with the program. No blocking issue here, but the spec should clarify that the NULL share for columns without an explicit NULL_SHARE entry defaults to (0.05, 0.20) as implemented.
issues.requested_revision: Document the default NULL share (0.05, 0.20) used for nullable columns not listed in NULL_SHARE, so the specification and program agree on the NULL share for all nullable columns.

unresolved_checks: Could not verify dependent-value consistency (FK values copied from final parent pools) because all units failed before any rows were written; the integrity check failure masks whether FK fills are correct.
Could not verify preservation of compact rows or reproducible generation because no instances were produced (n_instances=0).
Could not verify that intended value variation (boundary values, near-variants, group sizes, ties) remains possible in the written output, since no output was generated.

The spec's `supporting_evidence` for jobs.MAX_SALARY >= MIN_SALARY and employees.COMMISSION_PCT BETWEEN 0 AND 1 is consistent with the formulas in spec.py, but the actual generated values could not be inspected due to the integrity failure.

issues.evidence: Execution summary: n_ok=0, n_fail=20, errors={'rows_failed': 20}, rows_skipped={regions:62, countries:149, departments:191, jobs:142, employees:185, locations:107}. Every unit fails because write_instance_sqlite returns rows_failed>0 and cli._one sets res['err']='rows_failed'. The skipped rows are the generated rows that violate NOT NULL / PK / FK constraints when appended to the compact DB.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the writer/instance pipeline so generated rows are actually insertable: (a) generated PKs must not collide with compact PKs (e.g. offset generated integer PKs above max(compact PK) or dedup against the compact key set, not just within the generated batch); (b) NOT NULL columns (e.g. employees.LAST_NAME, EMAIL, HIRE_DATE, JOB_ID; departments.DEPARTMENT_NAME; jobs.JOB_TITLE; locations.CITY; job_history.START_DATE/END_DATE/JOB_ID) must never be NULL — the _apply_null_rule already skips notnull, but the samplers/planted values and the FK fill can still produce NULLs or duplicates; (c) FK values must be drawn from the final parent pool including compact rows. Re-run until n_fail=0 and rows_skipped all zero.

issues.evidence: instance.build_random_instance calls _apply_unmatched_parent AFTER _apply_null_rule and _apply_formulas, and _apply_unmatched_parent reserves the LAST row's PK tuple. But the reserved key is only excluded from _fk_pool for children generated later; the parent's own row is already fixed. More importantly, _apply_unmatched_parent is called per-table inside the loop, but _fk_pool reads spec.RESERVED_UNMATCHED which is cleared at the start of build_random_instance — however the reservation for a parent table happens only when that parent table is processed, which is before its children in topological order, so this part is OK. The real defect: _apply_null_rule runs before _apply_unmatched_parent and can NULL out a PK-adjacent column, and _apply_group_sizes / _apply_formulas run before _apply_unmatched_parent, so the 'last row' PK may be mutated by formulas (e.g. departments.DEPARTMENT_ID formula re-draw) after reservation is conceptually needed. Also _apply_group_sizes on job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID (a PK column of job_history) is skipped by the `gc in tm.primary_key` guard, so the spec target group_sizes for job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID is never enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder so _apply_unmatched_parent reserves keys before any child FK fill and before formulas/group-sizes can mutate the reserved row; and either implement group_sizes for job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID by controlling how many job_history rows share each employee (a non-PK-overwrite approach, e.g. choosing employee ids with multiplicities 1,2,>=3) or document that this target is intentionally dropped. Currently the spec lists job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID group_sizes but the code silently skips it.

issues.evidence: spec.NULL_FK_CHILD = {('employees','DEPARTMENT_ID')} only. The atomic-operation extraction lists child_rows_with_null_fk for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID (joins_with employees.DEPARTMENT_ID) and employees.DEPARTMENT_ID (joins_with departments.DEPARTMENT_ID). The spec per_column_exceptions list 'unmatched_join_rows' targets ['parent_rows_without_children','child_rows_with_null_fk'] for both departments.DEPARTMENT_ID and employees.DEPARTMENT_ID. Only employees.DEPARTMENT_ID is planted; departments.DEPARTMENT_ID is a PK and cannot be NULL, so the 'child_rows_with_null_fk' target for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID is unsatisfiable and should be dropped from the spec rather than silently ignored.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: remove the impossible 'child_rows_with_null_fk' target from departments.DEPARTMENT_ID (PK cannot be NULL) and keep it only for employees.DEPARTMENT_ID. Engineer: ensure NULL_FK_CHILD matches the corrected spec.

issues.evidence: values._spec_elements plants DUP_DISTINCT values as the literal string 'Manager' for every column in spec.DUP_DISTINCT, including employees.LAST_NAME and employees.PHONE_NUMBER. For PHONE_NUMBER the planted value 'Manager' violates the phone pattern 'NNN.NNN.NNNN' and the declared varchar(20) semantics; for LAST_NAME it is acceptable but arbitrary. Also TIE_ORDER plants 'Ontario'/'Yukon' for locations.STATE_PROVINCE regardless of the actual column, which is fine for a tie but not derived from the compact data.
issues.requested_revision: Make DUP_DISTINCT planting type-aware: for PHONE_NUMBER plant a valid phone-shaped duplicate (e.g. '555.0100' repeated), for LAST_NAME a name-shaped duplicate. Do not inject a single generic string into every duplicate-distinct column.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_formulas re-draws a violating value by choosing from `pool = [x for x in cols[cm.name] if x is not None]`, i.e. it copies another existing value in the same column. For PK columns (e.g. departments.DEPARTMENT_ID, locations.LOCATION_ID, regions.REGION_ID) this can create duplicate PKs after sample_fresh_primary_keys already deduped, and the writer then fails those rows (contributing to rows_skipped). The formula for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID (>0) and locations.LOCATION_ID (>0) is applied after PK dedup.
issues.requested_revision: Apply formulas before PK dedup, or make formula re-draws for PK columns generate fresh unique values (e.g. next integer above current max) rather than copying an existing value. Ensure the final PK set is deduped after all formula enforcement.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_null_rule sets NULL on every nullable column including employees.DEPARTMENT_ID, employees.MANAGER_ID, departments.MANAGER_ID, departments.LOCATION_ID, job_history.DEPARTMENT_ID, locations.COUNTRY_ID, countries.REGION_ID. This is consistent with the NULL rule. However _plant_child_fk_nulls runs after _apply_null_rule and only plants a NULL if none exists; combined with _revalidate_fks running before _apply_null_rule, a NULL planted by _apply_null_rule in a FK column is fine, but a FK value that was re-drawn by _revalidate_fks to a reserved-unmatched key is not re-checked after _apply_unmatched_parent. Ordering: _revalidate_fks -> _apply_null_rule -> _plant_child_fk_nulls -> _apply_group_sizes -> _apply_formulas -> _apply_unmatched_parent. The unmatched-parent reservation happens last, so children already filled may reference the reserved key, defeating 'parent_rows_without_children'.
issues.requested_revision: Reserve unmatched parent keys BEFORE filling child FKs (i.e. before the child table is processed), or re-run _revalidate_fks after _apply_unmatched_parent to strip reserved keys from child FK columns. Currently the 'parent_rows_without_children' target is not guaranteed by construction as the docstring claims.

issues.evidence: The spec's uncertainty note says the compact DB contains invalid rows (job_history START_DATE '0000-00-00', employees MANAGER_ID 0, DEPARTMENT_ID 0/90/100 not in departments, locations COUNTRY_ID not in countries) and that generation enforces FK integrity and drops these. The writer's _integrity_ok compares violation sets and tolerates pre-existing violations, which is correct. But the execution feedback reports fk_violations=0, not_null_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0 on the written files — meaning the compact DB's pre-existing violations are not actually present in the copied file (or the check is not seeing them). This is a discrepancy between the spec's stated uncertainty and the observed integrity result.
issues.requested_revision: Designer: confirm whether the compact DB actually contains the listed violations; if it does not, remove the uncertainty note. If it does, the writer's violation comparison should be verified to actually detect them (the current _violations uses pragma foreign_key_check which requires foreign_keys=ON and may miss rows depending on SQLite version).

issues.evidence: construction_pairs: eligible=106, separated=34. Many boundary/aggregate targets are not separated because the generated rows fail to insert (n_ok=0), so no instance actually contains the planted boundary values. Once the rows_failed issue is fixed, re-check separation. Also spec.BOUNDARY_NUM for employees.DEPARTMENT_ID includes 39,40,41,69,70,71 but employees.DEPARTMENT_ID is a FK to departments.DEPARTMENT_ID; the FK fill overwrites these planted values with parent keys, so the boundary values are never present in the final column. Same for employees.JOB_ID (FK) and departments.LOCATION_ID (FK).
issues.requested_revision: For FK columns that also carry a comparison_boundary target (employees.DEPARTMENT_ID), ensure the parent table contains the boundary values (departments.DEPARTMENT_ID already has 69,70,71,89,90,91 but not 39,40,41) so the FK fill can draw them, or plant the boundary values in the parent and let the child FK reference them. Currently employees.DEPARTMENT_ID boundary 39,40,41 is unreachable because departments has no such PKs.

unresolved_checks: Whether the compact DB truly contains the pre-existing violations listed in the spec uncertainty (execution reports 0 violations).
Whether job_history.EMPLOYEE_ID group_sizes (1,2,>=3) can be satisfied without violating the (EMPLOYEE_ID, START_DATE) PK — needs a multiplicity-aware construction.
Whether the 'parent_rows_without_children' target is actually achieved given the ordering of _apply_unmatched_parent after child FK fill.
Whether boundary values 39,40,41 for employees.DEPARTMENT_ID can ever appear given the FK constraint to departments.

issues.evidence: Specification's supporting_evidence lists only 4 formulas (job_history.END_DATE>=START_DATE, jobs.MAX_SALARY>=MIN_SALARY, employees.COMMISSION_PCT BETWEEN 0 AND 1, employees.SALARY>=0). The other 7 formulas in semantic_rules_and_formulas (regions.REGION_ID IN (1,2,3,4), countries.REGION_ID IN (1,2,3,4), departments.DEPARTMENT_ID>0, jobs.MIN_SALARY>=0, employees.HIRE_DATE range, job_history.START_DATE range, locations.LOCATION_ID>0) have no sample rows cited. These are nevertheless implemented as Python lambdas in spec.FORMULAS and enforced in instance._apply_formulas; the ENUMS for regions/countries REGION_ID and the DateSampler's [1980-01-01,2010-12-31] window make them structurally satisfied.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: add sample rows to supporting_evidence for the remaining formulas so each rule has explicit evidence. Not blocking — the rules are enforced by construction and the execution feedback shows 0 integrity violations.

issues.evidence: The atomic-operations summary lists 'unmatched_join_rows' for departments.DEPARTMENT_ID with targets including 'child_rows_with_null_fk': true. The spec explicitly drops this impossible target (departments.DEPARTMENT_ID is a PK and cannot be NULL) and only keeps it on employees.DEPARTMENT_ID. This is a deliberate, documented deviation, not an error.
issues.requested_revision: None required; the deviation is justified and recorded in spec.py's docstring and uncertainty note.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_unmatched_parent reserves the LAST row's PK tuple per parent table and _fk_pool excludes it. However _apply_unmatched_parent runs on the freshly sampled cols BEFORE _offset_primary_keys and sample_fresh_primary_keys. If the last row is later dropped by PK/UNIQUE dedup (e.g. duplicate PK against compact set), the reserved key may not exist in the final parent table, so the 'parent row with no children' guarantee could silently fail. Execution feedback reports 0 integrity violations and 20/20 valid instances, so this did not manifest in the run, but the ordering is fragile.
issues.requested_revision: Move _apply_unmatched_parent to AFTER _offset_primary_keys and sample_fresh_primary_keys (i.e. reserve a key from the final surviving parent rows), or verify the reserved key survives dedup and re-reserve if not. This is a robustness fix, not a blocking error given the observed clean run.

issues.evidence: instance._apply_job_history_multiplicity calls _parent_pool(schema, {}, 'employees', 'EMPLOYEE_ID') with an empty instance dict, so it only sees compact employee ids, not generated ones. Since generated employees are appended and the spec says FK fill uses 'compact + generated', the job_history employee ids are drawn from a narrower pool than the FK fill.
